verdicts.evidence: An independent LP solver (audit_claim1.py) matches the closed-form adversarial optimum l_in + alpha*max(l_out-l_in,0) across 28,950 comparisons (exhaustive 2-label/2-action family plus 120 seeded 3-label cases, five alpha values) with max absolute error 1.42e-14, and a destructive control example confirms the out-of-set penalty changes the minimizing action as theory predicts.

The logbook explicitly states this claim was not attempted, noting that the finite discrete audits used for other claims do not satisfy the non-atomic feature-space assumption required for Proposition 3.1 and Theorem 3.3.

An exhaustive exchangeability audit (14,850 orbit/alpha checks over all permutation orbits for n+1 in {3,4,5,6}) confirms the finite-sample coverage bound to numerical precision, and fresh empirical runs on 20 COVID seeds and 20 BDD splits show mean miscoverage within 0.00244 of alpha across seven alpha values.

Evaluating official cached probabilities at a pinned commit, ROCP shows lower critical-mistake rates than RAC on COVID (e.g., 1.19%/10.59%/4.77% vs 1.54%/12.95%/5.94% under Lambda0) and zero critical mistakes under high-cost Lambda1 where RAC remains nonzero; on BDD, ROCP realized loss is 2.320±0.019 vs RAC 2.981±0.075 with reduced collision rates across hazard states.

overall: The logbook provides concrete computational and empirical evidence supporting Claims 1, 3, and 4, including independent LP verification of the minimax policy, exhaustive exchangeability checks plus real-data coverage runs, and cached-artifact evaluations on COVID and BDD showing reduced critical mistakes. Claim 2 is explicitly unaddressed because the finite discrete audits do not cover the non-atomic setting the claim requires.
